text:
maria: heads up — after we applied the tighter netpols to priv-edge yesterday, the keystore agent in onprem cluster-2 can't reach the KMS endpoint. errors in pod logs show connection timeout. anyone seen this pattern?

ana: saw something similar last month when we flipped egress-deny. did we add explicit egress for the keystore to the KMS IPs/ports? netpols deny by default. :thinking_face:

ben: can you paste the pod logs and the netpol yaml? that helps. also, are we using a VPC endpoint, or straight to public KMS?

maria: logs (excerpt):
```
2024-03-14T10:12:03Z keystore-agent error: dial tcp 52.94.23.10:443: i/o timeout
2024-03-14T10:12:03Z keystore-agent warn: falling back to cached-wrapper (stale = 12m)
```
netpol: `priv-edge-keystore-egress` (applied cluster-wide) — will paste full yaml in a sec. we are using AWS KMS via VPC endpoint in prod, but this onprem cluster relies on internet egress to the central KMS (we know this is suboptimal).

devops: thanks. common culprits: 1) netpol doesn't match the pod label selector (so rules don't apply), 2) egress to external IPs needs a CIDR allowlist, 3) iptables conntrack limit causing timeouts when netpols are enforced.

maria: netpol snippet:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: priv-edge-keystore-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

ana: ah — that ipBlock is only internal. KMS public IPs are outside 10.0.0.0/8. netpol is effectively stopping outbound to the KMS public address. we either need to add the KMS egress CIDRs or route via proxy/VPC endpoint.

ben: question: do we have a stable list of KMS egress IPs for the region? AWS publishes ranges but they change. recommended pattern: allow egress to the regional VPC endpoint (if using a private link) or to a fixed NAT/proxy IP and control that on the netpol.

maria: for this cluster we don't have private link. we do have a central egress proxy (10.8.0.12) — i missed updating the netpol to permit that. adding it should be simple.

sre-oncall: short-term mitigation: add an egress rule allowing the keystore agent to reach the proxy IP and port 3128, then confirm TLS passthrough. medium-term: we should stop relying on public KMS endpoints from onprem — either deploy local KMS proxy/agent or mirror keys via secure sync.

devops: +1 on using a single egress proxy. also add audit logs to capture which key requests are failing so we can triage regressions. maria — can you run `kubectl exec` to curl the proxy from the keystore pod? like:
```
kubectl exec -it keystore-agent-xxxx -- curl -v --proxy http://10.8.0.12:3128 https://kms.amazonaws.com/
```

maria: ran it, result: `Couldn't resolve host 'kms.amazonaws.com'` when going through proxy. direct curl outbound from node works. looks like proxy has DNS config issue. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

ana: that explains it. Netpol was right to force traffic through the proxy, but the proxy can't resolve the KMS hostname. two action items: fix proxy DNS, and add explicit netpol egress to the proxy IP.

security-bot: [alert] priv-edge-keystore-egress applied 2024-03-13T18:02:11Z; policy blocks outbound TCP:443 from 6 pods (app=keystore-agent) — blocked_count=24 last24h.

ben: also consider RBAC checklist: ensure the keystore agent's ServiceAccount has minimal RBAC for reading its own secrets but not for manipulating key policies. we've seen escalation when faulty agents run as cluster-admin.

maria: agreed. for this incident I've opened short ticket INF-4921 to: 1) patch proxy DNS, 2) update netpol to allow proxy IP, 3) add audit logs for keystore->kms failures, 4) run post-change vulnerability scan on keystore agent image.

sre-oncall: for the audit logs — capture TLS SNI and source pod labels where possible. if we can't capture SNI, at least log connection attempts + serviceaccount. that'll help incident response.

devops: extra note: when we re-open egress make sure we don't broaden ipBlock to 0.0.0.0/0. use narrowest scope: proxy IP or AWS-managed endpoint CIDR. also add a scripted check that validates keystore can reach KMS after netpol changes.

maria: will do. I'll push netpol patch and follow up here once proxy DNS is fixed. thanks all. :pray:
